earlier_scan.source_named: Drabbe, P. 1950. Twee dialecten van de Awju-taal (Sjiagha and Jenimu dialects = Edera Awyu); not available online; also Lebold, Kriens & Susanto 2013 SIL Edera District survey (sil.org 403).

sources.citation: Kriens, Ron & Randy Lebold. 2010. Report on the Wildeman River survey in Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2010-010.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Companion SIL survey (Glottolog attaches it to South/Asue Awyu); may carry further Awyu wordlists with stress marks and the team's transcription conventions; unlikely to state a stress rule but is the only other SIL document on this dialect area.

sources.citation: Boelaars, J. H. M. C. 1950. The linguistic position of south-western New Guinea. Leiden: E. J. Brill. xxiii + 217 pp. (Utrecht dissertation; Glottolog: 'overview, comparative, grammar sketch')
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 2234.104.2; Widener Library (offsite storage), call number KF 19825)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 2234.104.2; Widener Library (offsite storage), call number KF 19825
sources.note: Only a notation remark in the Introduction (seq 21-22): stress is shown typographically ('a bold lettertype indicates stress'; 'This notation is not meant to be the last word in connection with pitch, accent etc.') followed by 'Although we do not discuss the phonological items of these languages..'. The Auju chapter (seq 98-104) is morphology only (nouns, pronouns, numerals, verbs) for Pisa. The comparative summary (seq 143) repeats Drabbe's view that noun-noun compounds stress the first constituent 'in most languages' of the area. No word-stress placement or tone statement for any Awyu lect.

sources.citation: Drabbe, P. 1950. Twee dialecten van de Awju-taal (met kaartje). Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 106(1): 92-147. doi:10.1163/22134379-90002483
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2 (sounds), p. 96: 'De toon, die op een syllabe valt, lijkt veel op de Nederlandse klemtoon; we geven hem aan met een accent-grave.' -- i.e. stress exists, sounds like Dutch stress, and is marked word by word with a grave accent; NO rule for where it falls. Sec. 5 p. 97: N+N compounds have 'de toon op het eerste woord'; secs. 40-42 pp. 114-116: in hesternal/distant-past verb forms 'de toon valt op de tijdwijzer' (stress on the tense marker). On the identity of the variety: describes Sjiagha (Aboghoj at Gimikja) and Jenimu (Jaso at Kunubi) + Pisa; Glottolog files it under sout2941 South A…

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa (Kemendikdasmen). Peta Bahasa: 'Bahasa Awyu Meto (Awyu Metto)', Provinsi Papua (entry idb=301); with neighbouring entry 'Bahasa Awyu Laut' (idb=299). Online language map, accessed 2026-09-20.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. 'Southeast Awyu' and 'Awyu'. New Guinea World (Santa Fe Institute), online comparative site; pages downloaded 2026-09-20 (the 'Edera Awyu' subpage is empty).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sources section names Lebold, Kriens & Susanto (2013: 36-47) as the only Edera Awyu source; lexical-similarity table; correspondence tables quoting Edera (Bhakti, Yame) forms with the survey's stress marks (e.g. a'ni 'older sister', 'asɯ 'night', bu'sɯ 'village') -- secondhand wordlist data with mixed penult/final marks, no statement about stress or tone. Parent 'Awyu' page reconstructs Proto-Awyu segments only.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2020. The Greater Awyu Languages of West Papua. Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 2 phonology treats only Aghu ('weak accent on the last syllable'), Digul Wambon, Kombai, Korowai; Shiaxa/Yenimu data are taken from Drabbe 1950 and no stress statement is made for any Edera/South Awyu lect.

sources.citation: Wester, Ruth. 2014. A linguistic history of Awyu-Dumut: morphological study and reconstruction of a Papuan language family. PhD dissertation, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 1.1.1-1.1.2: all Shiaxa and Yenimu data come from Drabbe 1950; stress mentioned only for compound nouns (first member stressed, after Drabbe). Nothing on Edera Awyu word stress.

sources.citation: Lebold, Randy, Ronald Kriens & Yunita Susanto. 2013. A report on the Bamgi, Kia, and Lower Digul River language survey in Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2013-008. 52 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement. Appendix H (pp. 36ff) prints four 239-item Edera Awyu wordlists (Meto, Ujung Kia, Yame, Bhakti) in IPA with primary-stress marks (e.g. item 001 'head': Meto ˈxabaŋ, Yame xaˈbaŋ, Bhakti ˈxabaŋ) -- raw data only. Fn. 3 p. 3 and Appendix A pp. 24-25 document the c. 2002 split of Siagha-Yenimu [OSR] into South Awyu [aws] and Edera Awyu [awy]; village tables put the Ia (=Siagha) and Bamgi (=Yenimu) River villages, incl. Konebi (Jas), in South Awyu.
